page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 168.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory allocation of 42.0 GB per core. It also includes 472 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-threaded capabilities alongside moderate multi-core throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, as well as strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth tests for large blocks also show lower relative throughput, though database operations and Redis SET operations maintain average performance tiers.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a specialized resource profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory footprints but moderate parallel processing power, avoiding the expense of provisioning excess vCPUs just to acquire sufficient RAM. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and single-threaded analytical tasks.
